questions.q: Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? 24,33,44, 57,72,?
questions.solution:
The increments are successive odd numbers 9, 11, 13 and 15. Add 17 next: 72 + 17 = 89.
**Answer: 89**

questions.q: Q starts from Point A and drives s 14 km towards the South. He then takes a left turn, drives 10 km, turns  left and drives 9 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 7 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 5 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive to reach Point A again? (All t turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified.)
questions.solution:
North–south distances cancel: -14 + 9 + 5 = 0. East–west movement is 10 - 7 = 3 km east. He must go 3 km west to return to A.
**Answer: 3 km towards the West**

questions.q: RV11 is related to GK18 in a certain way. In the same way, DH29 is related to SW36. To which of the following options is PT22 related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Advance each letter fifteen places modulo the alphabet and add seven to the number. PT22 becomes EI29.
**Answer: EI29**

questions.q: If each vowel in the word ROMANCE is changed to the nearest consonant succeeding it in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the nearest vowel succeeding it in English alphabetical order, then which of the following letters is repeated twice in the new group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
The transformed letters are U, P, O, B, O, E, F. O appears twice, coming from the consonants M and N.
**Answer: O**

questions.q: If P means ×, Q means ÷, R means − and S means +, evaluate (32 P 4) R (21 P 5) S (9 Q 3) P 6.
questions.solution:
Replace the codes to obtain 32 × 4 - 21 × 5 + (9/3) × 6 = 128 - 105 + 18 = 41.
**Answer: 41**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: No bike is a car. All cars are planes. Conclusions (I) No plane is a bike. (II) All planes are cars.
questions.solution:
The statements exclude cars from bikes and place cars within planes. Planes outside cars may be bikes, and not every plane has to be a car. Neither conclusion follows.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: Some bulbs are sands. All bulbs are candles. Conclusion: (I) Some candles are bulbs. (II) No candle is a sand.
questions.solution:
All bulbs are candles and some bulbs are sands. Thus some candles are bulbs, and some candles are sands as well. Only conclusion I follows.
**Answer: Only conclusion (I) follows.**

questions.q: In this question, a statement is followed by two courses of action, numbered I and I1. You must assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the courses of action logically follow(s) for pursuing. Statement: Severe congestion is seen on the service road outside the apartment complex between 7.30 a.m. to 9 a.m. everyday due to many school buses from different schools picking up children from gate of the apartment complex. This is leading to a traffic jam, delaying many people travelling for work at this time. Courses of Action: (I) No school buses should be permitted on the service road from 7.30 a.m. to 9 a.m. (II) School buses should be permitted to enter the society gates.
questions.solution:
An outright bus ban would obstruct school transport, while allowing buses inside the complex assumes safe space and access not stated. Neither proposal follows as a justified action from the information given.
**Answer: Neither I nor II follows**

questions.q: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Which numbers should replace X and Y so that the pattern followed by the two numbers on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of : ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) X : 192 ::  34 : Y
questions.solution:
Multiply the first number by three and add 15. This gives 59 × 3 + 15 = 192 and 34 × 3 + 15 = 117. Therefore X = 59 and Y = 117.
**Answer: X= 59, Y = 117**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.)
questions.solution:
Three pairs shift both letters backwards by five. XF would become SA, not SC, so XF–SC is the odd pair.
**Answer: XF-SC**

questions.q: Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? FEB, KJG, POL, UTQ, ?
questions.solution:
Every letter advances five places. UTQ becomes ZYV, the next term.
**Answer: ZYV**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
The common rule is -4 for the first letter and +3 for the second. MK should become IN, so MK–IO does not fit.
**Answer: MK-IO**

questions.q: If each vowel in the word WEIGHT is changed to the letter immediately succeeding it in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the letter immediately preceding it in the English alphabetical order. Which of the following letters is repeated twice in the new group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
WEIGHT becomes V, F, J, F, G, S. The letter F appears twice.
**Answer: F**

questions.q: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 63 - 45 + 14 + (81 ÷ 9) × 4 + 18 × 3 = 114 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
questions.solution:
Exchange 14 and 18. The expression becomes 63 - 45 + 18 + (81/9) × 4 + 14 × 3 = 18 + 18 + 36 + 42 = 114.
**Answer: 14 and 18**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘SKATE' is coded as ^35186' and *TAKER' is coded as “51623'. What is the code for R' in the given code language?
questions.solution:
S, K, A, T and E in SKATE share all but one letter with TAKER. The additional letter R takes the additional code digit 2.
**Answer: 2**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F sits second to the right of C. D is an immediate neighbour ofE and F. A sits second to the left of B. What is the position of E with respect to C?
questions.solution:
Fix C, put F two places right, and fit D between E and F. The A–B relation completes the remaining seats. E lies second to C’s left.
**Answer: Second to the left**

questions.q: All 36 students in a class are standing in a row facing north. Preeti is 12th from the right end while Alisha is 22nd from the left end. How many people stand between Preeti and Alisha?
questions.solution:
Preeti is 36 - 12 + 1 = 25th from the left. Alisha is 22nd. Number between them = 25 - 22 - 1 = 2.
**Answer: 2**

questions.q: If each consonant in the word PASTRY is changed to the letter immediately preceding it in the English alphabetical order and each vowel is changed to the letter immediately succeeding it in the English alphabetical order, then how many vowels are present in the new group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
PASTRY becomes O, B, R, S, Q, X. Only O is a vowel, so the total is one.
**Answer: One**

questions.q: In the following  number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying g certain mathematical operations to the first number. Which numbers should replace X and Y so that the pattern followed by the two numbers on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of : ? X : 66 : : 9 : Y
questions.solution:
Square the first number and add two. Thus 8² + 2 = 66 and 9² + 2 = 83, giving X = 8 and Y = 83.
**Answer: X=8, Y = 83**

questions.q: In a certain code language, *DOTH' is coded as '3764' and *HOLD' is coded as *7943'. What is the code for ^T' in the given code language?
questions.solution:
D, O and H occur in both words and share codes 3, 4 and 7. The additional letter T uses the additional code 6.
**Answer: 6**

questions.q: Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? BDF, IKM, PRT, WYA.?
questions.solution:
Advance every letter seven alphabet places with wraparound. WYA becomes DFH.
**Answer: DFH**

questions.q: Seven people, B, C, D, E, F, G and K are sitting  in a straight line, facing north. Only f five people sit between B and K. G sits to the immediate left of K. Only one e person sits between G and E. D sits at some place to the left of F but at some place to the right of C. Who sits third from the left end of the line?
questions.solution:
From left to right the order is B, C, D, E, F, G, K. The third person from the left is D.
**Answer: D**

questions.q: A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the wife of B; A ÷ B means A is the father of B; A # B means A is the daughter of B. How is Q related to J if Q + R − P × S ÷ T − J + K?
questions.solution:
Q is R’s mother, and R is P’s brother, so Q is P’s mother. P is S’s wife, and S is the father of T and J. Hence P is J’s mother, making Q J’s maternal grandmother.
**Answer: Mother's mother**

questions.q: Select the triad which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two triads given below. Both triads follow the samepattern. GB-HC-JL PK-QL-SU
questions.solution:
The second pair advances both letters one place. The third advances the original first letter three places and second letter ten places. QL becomes RM and TV.
**Answer: QL-RM-TV**
